summary.headline: Max Healthcare Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR 3,219 crore and operating EBITDA 18% to INR 820 crore, with margin flat at 26.8%.
summary.overview: Network gross revenue grew 20% YoY to INR 3,219 crore and operating EBITDA grew 18% to INR 820 crore, with margin at 26.8%, similar to last year despite a 14% rise in operational beds. PAT rose 10% YoY to INR 448 crore, though the prior-year base was normalised for a INR 149 crore one-time tax gain. Oncology in-patient revenue share fell to 21% from 26% after CGHS rate revisions led to discontinuation of some high-value chemotherapy drugs. Management said the Max Smart Saket ramp-up drag on EBITDA is temporary, and it flagged uncertainty over the newly imposed trade margin cap on non-scheduled drugs, which it has not yet quantified.

Flat YoY despite 14% bed capacity increase
INR 292 crore to expansion, INR 195 crore dividend
vs INR 2,384 crore at June 2026; net debt/EBITDA below 1x

segments.name: Hospital network
segments.commentary: Gross revenue INR 3,219 crore with occupancy at 77%; OBDs up 13% YoY, and in-patient volume up about 12% with ARPP up 8%. Excluding oncology, gross revenue grew 25% and ARPP 11%.

segments.name: Max@Home
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 86 crore, up 37% YoY, across 16 service lines in 15 cities, with over 56% repeat transactions.

segments.name: Max Lab
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 66 crore, up 24% YoY, serving over 60 cities and more than 7 lakh patients in the quarter.

segments.name: Max Bhubaneswar (Kalinga Hospital, 66% owned)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 38 crore and EBITDA INR 4 crore in the quarter; renovation started, with first part rolling out by year end.

segments.name: Digital and international
segments.commentary: Digital revenue INR 1,099 crore (about 34% of revenue); website traffic 1.14 crore sessions, up 44% YoY. International revenue INR 307 crore, up 33%.

guidance_outlook: Remaining 140 beds at Max Smart (Saket) to be commissioned after Diwali puja; balance 205 beds at Max Nanavati and Max Smart also post Diwali.
Max Dwarka oncology block adds about 20 beds in Q3 FY27.
Management expects top-line growth to accelerate in Q3 and Q4 as the chemotherapy-discontinuation impact is lapped.
Gurugram Sector-56 (500 beds): phase commissioning to start by end FY27, likely opening 150-200 beds first; peak EBITDA loss estimated at INR 40-50 crore.
Zirakpur, Mohali (400 beds): commissioning by December 2027, with peak EBITDA loss around INR 30 crore; breakeven guided within about one year, and about six months as achieved at Dwarka.
INR 415 crore approved for 209 brownfield beds at Noida, Vaishali and BLK-Max, including an INR 85 crore MLCP at BLK; most capacity in 18-24 months.
capex_capacity: Total bed capacity about 6,200 in H1, up 20% YoY; 202 brownfield beds added in Q2 at Max Smart, Lucknow, Noida and Dwarka.

Upcoming: 100 beds at Max Lucknow over next 2 quarters; 85 beds Noida and 100 beds Nagpur by December 2027; 200 beds Pitampura and 400 beds Patparganj by FY29; 260 beds Dwarka, 271 beds Nanavati Phase 2, 450 beds Pune, 200 beds Vaishali Tower 3 and 400 beds Shaheed Path Lucknow Phase 1 by FY30.
Bhubaneswar: 250-bed phased renovation over 12-15 months, with a further 250-bed tower planned over 2-3 years.
H1 FY27 capex of INR 629 crore on expansion projects; INR 386 crore spent on acquisitions of Kalinga Hospital and Yerawada Properties (Pune).
Shaheed Path Lucknow awaits environmental clearance and building plans before construction starts.
demand_pricing: Institutional bed share fell to 29% from 34% a year ago, and CGHS revenue share is about 18.5%, down 300 bps YoY.

Oncology share of in-patient revenue fell to 21% from 26%, as high-value chemotherapy drugs were discontinued for institutional patients after CGHS rate revisions; this is a roughly INR 100 crore annual headwind, offset by a net INR 200 crore gain from CGHS price revisions.
Trade margin cap on non-scheduled drugs: impact on sales and EBITDA still being assessed; the matter is sub judice.

De-empanelled BLK (CGHS and Railways) in May and ECHS at Shalimar Bagh; management will decide at individual hospital level as CGHS pressure builds, and will seek empanelment for the new Gurugram hospital.
Cardiology grew 16% YoY, per management; non-oncology segments grew about 20% industry-wide per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the drag from the Max Smart Saket ramp-up, and will other brownfields see similar disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Saket drag is a one-quarter preoperative cost; Mohali and Nanavati broke even in the first quarter. Excluding Saket, revenue grew 20% and EBITDA 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Gurugram greenfield EBITDA impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will open 150-200 beds first, and peak EBITDA loss should be INR 40-50 crore, based on a INR 30 crore loss at Dwarka with 300 beds.

qa_highlights.question: Will the trade margin cap affect pharmacy revenue and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not yet estimated the impact. Chemotherapy is about 30% of oncology revenue, and part of it may be exempt through ORC or monopoly drugs. Pharmacy share of total revenue was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the top-line growth accelerate in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said growth should accelerate in Q3 and Q4 on a lower base, aided by new brownfield and greenfield beds.

qa_highlights.question: Could cardiology growth be slowing, and what is ex-oncology EBITDA growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cardiology is seasonal and grew 16% YoY. It declined to quantify ex-oncology EBITDA growth, saying the P&L cannot be adjusted for lost drug revenue.

risks_watch: Trade margin cap on non-scheduled drugs and the sub judice oncology pricing case: impact not quantified.
Further de-empanelment from CGHS or ECHS if capacity stays under pressure; institutional mix is falling as older hospitals shed it.
Gurugram Sector-56 and Zirakpur greenfield ramp-ups, with peak EBITDA losses of INR 40-50 crore and about INR 30 crore respectively.
Clinician attrition, estimated at about 1% per year, as new Gurugram capacity is staffed.
Occupancy at 77% despite 14% bed growth; watch whether ramp-ups keep pace with the 200+ beds coming online in the next few quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, ramp-ups and the growth outlook, with firm numbers on brownfield economics. Cautious and evasive on the trade margin cap, on pharmacy share of revenue and on hospital-level occupancy, saying the matter is sub judice or not disclosed.
key_quotes: Demand for quality healthcare remains strong across the hospital Network, with occupancy holding steady at 77%, despite a 14% year-on-year increase in operational bed capacity.
A brownfield breaks even within the first quarter itself.
We cannot have day one occupancy of 500 beds; it does not operate like that.

growth.why: Management expects top-line growth to accelerate in Q3 and Q4 as the oncology chemotherapy headwind is lapped, backed by about 225 beds due after Diwali and 20 beds at Dwarka in Q3, plus a 500-bed Gurugram greenfield starting by end FY27; no numeric revenue guide was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Operating EBITDA margin held at 26.8% (similar YoY, up ~200 bps QoQ), but Gurugram Sector-56 and Zirakpur greenfield peak losses of INR 40-50 crore and about INR 30 crore, plus an unquantified trade margin cap, cut against expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 225 beds come live after Diwali (140 at Max Smart Saket, 205 across Nanavati and Max Smart, overlapping) plus 20 Dwarka oncology beds in Q3, and 100 Lucknow beds over the next 2 quarters; Gurugram Sector-56 phase commissioning starts by end FY27 with 150-200 beds.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects top-line growth to accelerate in Q3 and Q4 on a lower oncology base, with in-patient volume up about 12% and OBDs up 13% YoY in Q2, though occupancy is flat at 77% despite 14% more beds.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 77% and not rising despite 14% bed growth, but the Board already approved INR 415 crore for 209 brownfield beds and 500-bed Gurugram and 400-bed Zirakpur greenfields are in the pipeline, so further announcements are probable as the pipeline runs into FY30.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Growth is expected to accelerate in Q3 and Q4 as the INR 100 crore oncology headwind is lapped, but no numeric revenue guide was given and Q2 revenue grew 20% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Trade margin cap on non-scheduled drugs is unquantified and sub judice, further CGHS or ECHS de-empanelment is possible, and the Gurugram ramp costs INR 40-50 crore at peak.

rows.label: Trade margin cap on non-scheduled drugs
rows.why: Impact on sales and EBITDA is not yet quantified and the matter is sub judice; chemotherapy is about 30% of oncology revenue and part may be exempt.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA below 1x with Q2 FCF of INR 500 crore
rows.why: Net debt fell to INR 2,369 crore from INR 2,384 crore, and net debt/EBITDA is below 1x even after INR 292 crore of expansion spend and INR 195 crore of dividend in Q2.

rows.label: Max Smart Saket ramp-up drag fading
rows.why: Management calls the Saket drag a one-quarter preoperative cost, and Mohali and Nanavati broke even in their first quarter; ex-Saket revenue grew 20% and EBITDA 25%.

tone.note: Management was confident on brownfield ramp-ups, the H2 growth acceleration and Gurugram economics, but cautious and evasive on the unquantified trade margin cap, pharmacy revenue share and ex-oncology EBITDA growth; analysts probed those areas.
